rationale: While the core neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variants affecting the CxxC DNA-binding domain of KDM2B demonstrates nearly 100% penetrance for developmental delay (predominantly affecting speech and motor domains) and a 50-78% frequency of congenital heart defects (such as ASD and VSD), comprehensive assessment across the broader molecular spectrum of KDM2B variants reveals significant incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity for loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants. Furthermore, individuals with 12q24.31 microdeletions show lower rates of congenital heart defects (3/12, or 25%). Consequently, the hypothesis that developmental delay is present in virtually 100% of all reported individuals with KDM2B-related disorder is true for CxxC hotspot variants, but contradicted by incomplete penetrance observed in non-CxxC and loss-of-function variants.

evidence.text: All 19 individuals with KDM2B CxxC variants presented with developmental delay, primarily affecting motor and speech domains, alongside variable intellectual disability. Congenital heart defects were observed in up to 78% of these individuals.

source.title: KDM2B variants in the CxxC domain impair its DNA-binding ability and cause a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: All individuals with CxxC variants presented with developmental delay, mainly in the speech and motor domain, in addition to variable intellectual disability and mild facial dysmorphism. Congenital heart defects were observed in up to 78% of individuals, with additional common findings including musculoskeletal, ophthalmological, and urogenital anomalies, as well as behavioral challenges and feeding difficulties.

evidence.text: Comprehensive assessment of 68 individuals (with 47 pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants) confirmed a highly penetrant phenotype specifically in CxxC domain variants, whereas loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants exhibited incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity. Congenital heart defects were observed in only 3 of 12 individuals with 12q24.31 microdeletions.

source.title: Comprehensive Assessment of the KDM2B‐Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorder and the 12q24. 31 Microdeletion Syndrome
source.quote: In contrast, our findings point to variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance of loss-of-function variants and JmjC domain variants complicating variant classification and genetic counseling. We identify KDM2B as a strong contributor to the 12q24.31 microdeletion syndrome, while also addressing the role of additional genes in the region.

numbers.metric: Congenital heart defects in 12q24.31 microdeletion cohort

evidence.text: A case series of 3 individuals with CxxC domain variants confirmed global developmental delay and speech/motor delays in 3/3, with congenital heart disease (atrial septal defect and/or ventricular septal defect) present in 2/3 individuals.

source.title: KDM2B‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder A Case‐Series Supporting the CxxC Domain Phenotype With Emphasis on Ocular and Dermatologic Features
source.quote: Patient 1 is a 2-year-old boy with developmental delay, solitary kidney, atrial septal defect, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism. Patient 2 is a 2-year-old girl with global developmental delay, hip dysplasia, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism. Patient 3 is a 5-year-old girl with autism, developmental delay, atrial septal defect, and ventricular septal defect, hypertrichosis, atopic dermatitis, and myopic astigmatism.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 21 individuals with heterozygous (likely) pathogenic KDM2B variants, individuals presented with developmental delay and/or intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, subtle facial dysmorphism, and congenital organ anomalies mainly of the heart, eyes, and urogenital system.

source.title: Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and its associated DNA methylation signature
source.quote: Individuals in this cohort present with developmental delay and/or intellectual disability; autism; attention deficit disorder/attention deficit hyperactivity disorder; congenital organ anomalies mainly of the heart, eyes, and urogenital system; and subtle facial dysmorphism.

conflicts: CxxC domain variants show full (>95-100%) penetrance of developmental/speech delay and high CHD prevalence (50-78%), whereas loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants demonstrate incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity.
Congenital heart defects occur in up to 78% of CxxC variant carriers and 66% (2/3) of small series, but were reported in only 25% (3/12) of 12q24.31 microdeletion cases.

new_directions.question_text: What are the specific penetrance rates and cardiac defect frequencies for truncating vs missense non-CxxC KDM2B variants compared to CxxC domain variants?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying domain-specific genotype-phenotype correlations will resolve whether the high penetrance of neurodevelopmental delay and CHD is strictly confined to CxxC variants acting through dominant negative or altered binding mechanisms rather than simple haploinsufficiency.

new_directions.question_text: Does machine-learning episignature profiling reliably differentiate KDM2B CxxC-domain variants from KDM2B loss-of-function variants and other Mendelian chromatinopathies?
new_directions.rationale: Sub-episignatures specific to the CxxC domain have been detected; establishing their specificity relative to overlapping disorders (e.g., SETD1B, KDM6B, KMT2B) would allow definitive laboratory diagnosis when phenotypic overlap is present.
